children: Jefferies junks an expectation for a special dividend from Westpac when it reports annual earnings on Nov. 2. Instead, analyst Andrew Lyons assumes Westpac retains its elevated payout. Jefferies forecasts flat cash earnings of A$6.96 billion in FY26, slightly below consensus hopes for A$7.0 billion. It thinks strong volume growth will be offset by pressure on net interest margin and higher bad debts. "Focus into FY27 shifts to three key debates: margin upside from higher rates, whether above-system Business growth can be sustained and cost discipline," Jefferies says. It retains a hold call, raises its price target by 0.8% to A$34.99/share. Westpac ended Tuesday at A$35.13. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
